supporting_quotes.exact: In computer science, an array is a data structure consisting of a collection of elements (values or variables), of the same memory size, each identified by at least one array index or key, the collection of which may be a tuple, known as an index tuple.

observations.subject: array (in computer science)
observations.object: data structure consisting of a collection of elements (values or variables) of the same memory size, each identified by at least one array index or key, the collection of which may form an index tuple

supporting_quotes.exact: In general, an array is a mutable and linear collection of elements with the same data type. An array is stored such that the position (memory address) of each element can be computed from its index tuple by a mathematical formula. The simplest type of data structure is a linear array, also called a one-dimensional array.

observations.subject: array
observations.object: mutable and linear collection of elements with the same data type; element position (memory address) computable from index tuple by a mathematical formula; linear (one-dimensional) array is the simplest data structure

supporting_quotes.exact: Arrays are useful mostly because the element indices can be computed at run time.
For that reason, the elements of an array data structure are required to have the same size and should use the same data representation.

supporting_quotes.exact: In systems which use processor cache or virtual memory, scanning an array is much faster if successive elements are stored in consecutive positions in memory, rather than sparsely scattered. This is known as spatial locality, which is a type of locality of reference.

observations.subject: scanning an array
observations.object: successive elements stored in consecutive positions in memory rather than sparsely scattered

qualifiers.context: systems which use processor cache or virtual memory
qualifiers.called: spatial locality, a type of locality of reference

claims.rationale: 引文文本区间 0..267 完整覆盖 claim：①限定条件为使用处理器缓存或虚拟内存的系统；②相继元素连续存储（而非稀疏散布）时扫描更快；③该性质称为空间局部性（spatial locality），是引用局部性（locality of reference）的一种。claim 中每个成分均有对应原文，无附加断言，判定 supported。provenance 为空，无法举证独立性，independence 记为 independence_unknown。

supporting_quotes.exact: Many algorithms that use multidimensional arrays will scan them in a predictable order. A programmer (or a sophisticated compiler) may use this information to choose between row- or column-major layout for each array.
For example, when computing the product A·B of two matrices, it would be best to have A stored in row-major order, and B in column-major order.

observations.object: programmer (or sophisticated compiler) to choose between row- or column-major layout for each array

observations.subject: product A·B of two matrices
observations.object: A stored in row-major order and B in column-major order
